chunks: He said: Abu Ghalib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zurari, may God have mercy on him, informed me, saying: My maternal uncle Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Buraid ibn Mu'awiya al-Ajali, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his forefathers, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him and his family, said:

God, Most High, says: Grace is a gift from Me to My believing servant. If he accepts it from Me, then it is by My mercy and from Me. And if he rejects it, then due to his sin he is deprived of it, and it is from him, not from Me. And whichever servant I created, and I guided him to faith, and made good his character, and did not afflict him with miserliness -- for indeed I intend good for him.

key_terms.المعروف: Grace, recognized good, acts of kindness -- a comprehensive Quranic term for all that is known and recognized as virtuous in God's sight
key_terms.بخل: Miserliness, stinginess -- considered a spiritual affliction that God withholds from those He favors
key_terms.خلق: Character, moral disposition -- the innate ethical nature that God fashions in His servants
key_terms.هدية: A gift -- here indicating that divine grace is not earned but bestowed as a gift from God

ai.seo_question: What does God say about grace and generosity being His gift to believers in this Hadith Qudsi?
ai.summary: In this Hadith Qudsi (sacred narration) from al-Amali of al-Mufid, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) conveys God's words about the nature of divine grace. God declares that al-ma'ruf (grace, kindness) is His gift to His believing servants. If a servant accepts this gift, it flows from God's mercy; if he rejects it, the deprivation is due to his own sin, not from God. Furthermore, God explains that any servant He has created, guided to faith, and blessed with good character -- and has not afflicted with miserliness -- is one for whom God intends good. This narration was transmitted through a chain of distinguished scholars and Imams, reaching back from Imam al-Baqir (AS) through his forefathers to the Prophet. The original audience of this teaching understood 'al-ma'ruf' in its rich Quranic sense -- not merely kindness, but the totality of recognized good that God facilitates through His servants, including generosity, hospitality, and fulfilling the rights of others.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 1. He said: Abu Ghalib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zurari, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his maternal uncle Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Razzaz al-Qurashi, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Jamil ibn Swaleh, from Barid ibn Mu’awiyah al-Ajali, from Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon him, from his forefathers, that: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said

Allah, Most High, says: "Grace and Blessing are My gift to My believing servant. If he accepts them, that is My mercy and from Me. And if he rejects them, that is because of his sins which deprive him; and it is his doing and not Mine. And I have guided every creature to Faith, and fashioned him in a shapely manner. And I never made him a victim of miserliness, for I always wished him good."
